reviews.title: little by little, then all at once
reviews.text:
for my whole life, my father has gotten a physical copy of the NYT delivered every single day. he still does. around 20 years ago, during the worst period of my life (and no, it was not rehab, a psych ward, or prison) I had been given the “privilege” of communicating by letter with my father..he would send me articles every single one of the miserable 353 days I was there (after around 6 weeks to ensure I was “broken” enough) and sometimes it was used to send coded messages from a code we had made up when I was a kid..other times it was just interesting things, and I would reply with my opinion. my letters, received and sent, were heavily searched and studied (ESPECIALLY the ones I sent) but it helped keep me sane.
The NYT of today is practically unrecognizable. You can still find at least one gem per paper, but most of the articles should be labeled as “op-ed” … it leans hard left. Unless it’s an op-ed, I want facts, not propaganda..from real journalists. Not…fanfiction.

reviews.title: Unacceptable
reviews.text:
Prolonged neglect means my review has gone down to 1 star. The people in charge of this app should be fired. How does this app not work well offline after so many years? And how does it not remember what you have read and personalize based on it? Captive audience means no incentive to make this better. Shame.

Previous 2-star review:

The memory pressure crashes in a loop have gotten fairly frequent and ridiculous. My suspicion is the ads are given free reign in terms of memory. But wouldn’t be surprised if the app itself does not manage it well. In general, this app stores an excessive amount of data, even with the setting to not do so. Have to delete it every once in a while to reclaim. And the scrolling being messed up by ads loading and expanding the page has always been an issue. The devs can’t figure out how to prioritize current scroll position.

Otherwise, I am very happy with the reporting and the service. It’s just the app that’s subpar.

reviews.title: Home Delivery
reviews.text: My family and I have been receiving the physical newspaper for over 40 years, and only since moving to a new address have I had trouble with the delivery person, who refuses to bring the newspaper inside the apartment building for 55+. Several times the newspaper has been stolen because the paper is not brought inside the locked lobby, but rather thrown on the stoop in the elements outside of the building. Though the Times  has not yet suffered journalistically, Customer Service is deplorable.  Instead of “re-delivering” (NYT’s term) the physical newspaper, they have offered to refund a discounted amount.  I have told several managers on the customer service 800-number that I am paying to have the old faithful newspaper delivered, not to get a paltry refund for poor service. No wonder that most newspapers have closed operations and production in this disposable world. The sun is setting on the Grey Lady, it seems.

reviews.title: Poor audio options
reviews.text:
NYT purchased Audm and ran it as the NYT audio app, which was a great platform with human narrated stories and articles from many sources. It shut down the audio app and now the nyt app is worse than nothing from an audio standpoint. It does not even have narrated articles on its audio section, and the narrated articles that do exist are AI voices. Perhaps the owners of the voices used to train those bots feel similarly to nyt writers who sued ai companies for the use of their text. Regardless, the quality is poor.

The practice of buying a competing news app and then shutting it down is anticompetitive trust-like behavior. I frankly don’t want to hear old Sulzberger, in an ad, sanctimoniously telling me to support local newspapers when this is the practice of his own company. 

I now get my podcasts from the nyt on my podcast app, and read fewer articles because there are no easily available narrated options. I also get nothing from the myriad of sources that I once was able to access on the audio app. So much for supporting other news orgs.

Also, on a separate note, it is tedious to find the “New York” section of the times, and even then, not much municipal news is covered. If you’re not covering many stories, you cede ground to the Post. There is a large appetite for granular coverage of the Mandani admin. 

Both of this omission, and the killing of audm, ironically, have led me to support other local journalism like streetsblog, hellgate, etc.

So why spoil a good package for subscribers with increasingly more annoying advertising:  more frequent, more irrelevant, larger and more distracting.  Logging into the website is even more annoying as I get rebuked for not accepting their ‘generous’ discount family upgrade.  So presumptuous are these sales cowboys.

I was fine to give them my email but them asking me to give them money on a card (which I do not even have by the way) is ridiculous and pushy! I would just like to get my project done but I guess because of New York Times I will just have to fail it! People running New York Times, even if I did want to subscribe to read 1 article, how would you expect me to do it if I don’t have a card? Go out and get a card, put money on it, and then give you that money on a subscription that I’m most likely to never go into again? I’m beyond upset because something that should just be so simple to read, I now have to try to quickly take pictures of the article, reloading it and trying to find where I left off as fast as I can before the subscription stub comes up again!
